title: Multi-Camera Rendering
summary: Official Derivative overview of rendering multiple cameras in a single render pass through Render TOP camera lists, including GPU support requirements, VR/cube-map use cases, light-mask limitations, Multi-Camera Hint, and Render Select TOP extraction.
guidance: Use this article when a Render TOP should render several cameras looking at the same scene efficiently.
Multi-camera rendering traverses the scene graph once and avoids repeated driver work for shared lights, textures, materials, and draw calls.
Use it for VR-style camera pairs or cube-map rendering where a single pass is preferable to one pass per camera or cube side.
Multi-camera rendering will not function when cameras have different light masks; those cameras render one pass at a time.
In Render TOP, list multiple cameras in the Cameras parameter, tune behavior with Multi-Camera Hint, and use Render Select TOP to extract each camera result.
